description: Fix two CPS runtime bugs: (1) recursive procs with suspending bodies produce <error: error>, (2) set mutation inside concurrent CPS closures silently fails due to per-worker VM isolation.

userStories.title: Diagnose and fix recursive CPS suspension error
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need to find and fix the code path that produces <error: error> when a recursive proc body contains suspending operations (spawn/await/parallel).
acceptanceCriteria: Create a minimal .jacl reproducer in test/jacl/cps_recursive_spawn.jacl that demonstrates the bug (recursive proc with spawn/await in body)
Trace through compiler__compile_suspending_call_cps() for the recursive call — identify whether the issue is in tail-call continuation passing or upvalue capture in compiler__emit_continuation()
Trace runtime execution through runtime__spawn_task_exec / runtime__continuation_task_exec — identify where jacl_set_error(jacl_inline_string("error", 5)) gets triggered
Fix the root cause in compiler.c and/or runtime.c so recursive procs with suspending bodies return correct results
Document the root cause and fix rationale in a comment near the changed code
Existing CPS tests all pass (cps_*.jacl, spawn_*.jacl, parallel_*.jacl)
All existing tests pass
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: The likely culprit is compiler__compile_suspending_call_cps() in compiler.c (around lines 1141-1199). When remaining_count == 0 (tail call), the compiler passes the parent's __k directly. For recursive calls where the body creates intermediate continuations, this chain may not thread results back correctly. The <error: error> is generated at runtime.c lines ~1094 and ~1177 when vm__run() doesn't return VM_OK or the continuation wasn't properly called.

userStories.notes: JACL proc names must be <= 7 bytes. Use short names like 'work', 'loop', 'recur'. == is the equality operator (not =). Use def not set in concurrent mode. The test harness auto-discovers .jacl files in test/jacl/.

userStories.title: Diagnose and handle set mutation in concurrent CPS closures
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need to fix or explicitly restrict set inside concurrent CPS closures so that silent data loss doesn't occur.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm the root cause: per-worker vm->env isolation in runtime__init_worker_vm() means OP_SET_GLOBAL only modifies the local worker's env
Implement a compile-time error: compiler.c emits an error when set targets a variable inside a spawn/parallel/race body in CPS mode
Error message clearly tells the user to use def instead
Document the rationale in a comment near the check (per-worker VM isolation makes cross-worker mutation unsound)
Existing CPS and mutation tests pass (mut_*.jacl files must still work in single-threaded mode)
All existing tests pass
build.sh passes
Compiles without warnings
userStories.notes: Approach revised: instead of compile-time error, set! inside concurrent bodies triggers worker pinning. The compiler scans for set! in concurrent body ASTs and marks closures as pinned. At runtime, pinned tasks are pushed to the owning worker's private deque instead of the global inbox. This ensures OP_SET_GLOBAL modifies the correct vm->env. Phase 1b pre-registers mut declarations so proc bodies can resolve mutable globals.
